record.original_question: Let G be a graph of order n with clique number omega. Is it always true that sqrt(s+(G)) <= (1 - 1/omega)n, where s+(G) is the sum of the squares of the positive adjacency eigenvalues of G?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2 (Elphick-Wocjan [56]). Let G be a graph of order n with clique number ω. Then sqrt(s+(G)) ≤ (1 − 1/ω)n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices with adjacency matrix $A(G)$, and let $\lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2 \ge \cdots \ge \lambda_n$ denote the eigenvalues of $A(G)$. Define
$$s^{+}(G) = \sum_{\lambda_i > 0} \lambda_i^2,$$
the sum of the squares of the positive adjacency eigenvalues of $G$. Let $\omega = \omega(G)$ denote the clique number of $G$. Prove or disprove that for every such graph $G$,
$$\sqrt{s^{+}(G)} \le \left(1 - \frac{1}{\omega}\right) n.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The inequality is the Elphick–Wocjan conjecture (2018), a spectral strengthening of Turán's theorem. It has been verified for several classes (triangle-free graphs, weakly perfect graphs, Kneser graphs, conference graphs, certain strongly regular and Ramanujan graphs, and almost all graphs), and no counterexamples have been found computationally up to 40 vertices, but the conjecture remains open in general as of recent works (2024–2025).

status_evidence.title: Conjectured lower bound for the clique number of a graph
status_evidence.snippet: Elphick and Wocjan conjecture n/(n - sqrt(s+)) ≤ ω, equivalent to sqrt(s+) ≤ (1 - 1/ω)n.

status_evidence.title: Conic programming to understand sums of squares of eigenvalues of graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work studying s+(G) and related conjectures; conjecture remains a topic of active investigation.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture treated as still open in 2024.

status_evidence.title: Strengthening Wilf's lower bound on clique number
status_evidence.snippet: 2025 paper discussing strengthenings of clique-number bounds including the Elphick-Wocjan conjecture, treating it as open in general.
